title: A signal from the Moon
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Light takes a little over a second to travel from the Moon to Earth. Even nearby astronomical views show the object slightly in the past.

misconception: A learner may choose: Yes: light has no travel time
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: If the Moon changed abruptly, would an observer on Earth see the change at exactly the same instant?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: If the Moon changed abruptly, would an observer on Earth see the change at exactly the same instant? No: its light takes time to travel. Light takes a little over a second to travel from the Moon to Earth. Even nearby astronomical views show the object slightly in the past.
Visual caption: Moon to Earth takes time. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: If the Moon changed abruptly, would an observer on Earth see the change at exactly the same instant?
options: Only if the Moon is full
No: its light takes time to travel
Yes: light has no travel time
recall.why: Light takes a little over a second to travel from the Moon to Earth. Even nearby astronomical views show the object slightly in the past.
